scripts: Evaluated model

Good morning sir. This is my Phase 2 progress review. I evaluated Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with the final Pavlov adapter trained through Tinker, using seed 809. The current work covers fourteen public benchmarks. I will show the results, the evaluation conditions, and the work still pending.
ZVF and research context

The research starts with a simple observation: when every answer in a training group receives the same reward, subtracting the group average leaves no reward contrast. The ZVF work studies that condition. This context relates to NeurIPS 2026 submission 36320. The earlier Qwen3-8B study and today’s larger adapted model are separate experiments. No submission outcome or causal capability gain is asserted.
Verified results

There are three strictly complete suites and one additional official result with parser exclusions. LAB-Bench is 450 out of 1,967, or 22.88 percent. AgentDojo benign utility is 88 out of 97, or 90.72 percent. VerilogEval is 129 out of 312, or 41.35 percent. Omni-MATH is 2,271 out of 4,426 accepted reports, or 51.31 percent. Two reports were excluded by the original parser, so the strict 4,428-report score remains unavailable.
E1 to E7

Today I resolved the remaining six SWE-bench Multilingual image configurations. All 300 metadata records now pass the original strict audit. This completes image metadata recovery, while image execution and model patches remain pending. CORE-Bench has one of 45 original capsules prepared. MLAgentBench still needs its released evaluator and weights. BankerToolBench needs the actual banking deliverables and grading. Tau3 Banking has all 698 documents indexed and all 97 native initializations checked. Two native attempts, including one with a replacement key, each received three OpenAI credit-exhaustion errors. No episode completed. After the credit reload, the native GPT-4.1 provider returned a successful availability response. Full native evaluation remains pending. WebArena still needs its live sites. CyberGym still needs the native task payload and verifier.
E8 to E14

This table covers the remaining public suites. LAB-Bench, AgentDojo and VerilogEval have complete native results. Omni-MATH now has an official result with two parser exclusions. MLDevBench has all 374 released files. Twelve of its fourteen previously unbound starting states use native directory creation. One generates random logs and one still needs a runtime workspace prerequisite checked. Runtime validation and all 34 native runs remain pending. VisualAgentBench lacks 284 original task assets. BALROG completed 13 of 255 episodes with the exact trained BF16 actor and verified native environments. The native run stopped after an action call failed all five retries. Some model responses exhausted the native token limit without a final action. This is a partial run, so the full-suite score remains unavailable.
LAB-Bench

The model answered 450 of 1,967 questions correctly: 22.88 percent native accuracy. The chart shows complete category results. Saved diagnostics include answer formatting and length limits, but they do not establish a quantified causal explanation for the errors.
AgentDojo

The model passed 88 of 97 benign utility episodes: 90.72 percent. This measures ordinary user-task completion, not prompt-injection security. The final result preserves the original attempts and a documented continuation that completed the remaining episodes.
Verilog

The retained result passed 129 of 312 native checks: 41.35 percent. It was generated with the original Tinker sampler. The chart separates two 156-task framings. No new Verilog samples were taken, and this result does not establish an improvement over an unmeasured baseline.
Omni-MATH

Omni-MATH has 4,428 fixed policy answers and 4,428 saved judge responses. The original Omni-Judge parser accepts 4,426 reports and excludes two truncated reports. It marks 2,271 accepted answers correct, giving 51.31 percent. Today I reran the unchanged native scorer, checked the saved file hashes, and matched every one of the 4,428 saved task dispositions. I did not retry the excluded reports or change their grades. The expanded native-input audit now verifies 42,408 files. Historical budget references resolve to byte-identical saved snapshots; unrelated temporary log archives remain explicitly labeled as non-input historical records. The strict full-suite score remains unavailable.
Model and execution provenance

The policy is the exact Qwen3.6 base with the final Pavlov adapter. LAB-Bench, AgentDojo and Omni-MATH answers used the merged BF16 weights. VerilogEval used the original Tinker sampler. Omni-Judge is the separate math grader, with the later grading campaign on Modal A100. A fresh metadata request today still returns checkpoint not found for the original sampler. No numerical parity between serving backends is claimed.
Evaluation conditions

LAB-Bench combined 240 eager-serving responses, 1,504 graph-serving responses at 32,768-token context, and 223 at 65,536-token context. Original answers were retained. The source-overlap checks cover a defined source envelope, not images, semantic similarity or universal pretraining exposure.
What the measurements mean

Each score has its own meaning and denominator. LAB-Bench measures question accuracy. AgentDojo measures benign task completion. VerilogEval measures pass at one over two task framings. Omni-MATH uses the separate judge and its accepted-report denominator. These scores should not be averaged or interpreted as improvement over an unmeasured baseline.
Runtime repairs and remaining execution

The main update is that the original Omni-MATH scoring now reproduces locally, and SWE-bench image metadata recovery is complete for all 300 tasks. Three suites meet the full strict requirements. Omni-MATH has an official result with two exclusions. The other ten public suites still need model execution or missing native assets. BALROG completed 13 of 255 episodes after runtime recovery, then stopped on a native action failure. Tau3 API funding is now available and its full native evaluation remains pending. The full scores for these suites remain unavailable. The remaining work is to complete native execution and recover the missing original assets.
